Lesson 36. Compound Intervals

Intervals whose notes are more than one octave apart are known as compound intervals. The compound second (an octave plus a second) becomes a ninth, a compound third becomes a tenth, a compound fourth becomes an eleventh, and so on. The terms perfect, major, and minor still apply, as though the notes were in the same octave.

M9 M10 P11 P12 M13 M14 P15 m9 m10 P11 P12 m13 m14 P15

Practice

1. Write the indicated interval above each given note.

M9 m10 P11 P12 M13 m14 P15

2. Write the indicated interval below each given note.

M9 M10 P11 P12 M13 M14 m9

3. Identify each interval with its complete compound name.
